beats: Hook: two states differ only by a minus sign. In one case (|+> against -|+>) no experiment in the universe can tell them apart; in the other (|+> against |->) a single measurement can. Where does the sign sit? (line_qc_phase_dancers.) A 2024-only part: primary Q24-08 53:32-72:49 (in-person recording: check every clip for student voices and room noise).

Measured, result unknown (Q24-08 53:49-58:22): a coin that has landed under a cup is heads or tails, we just don't know which: a mixture, written as a density matrix rho = sum p_i |psi_i><psi_i|. A spinning coin is not secretly heads or tails (line_qc_mix_spin_or_cup). Honest caveat: a real spinning coin is classical; here it only stands in for the definite state |+>.

The test that tells them apart: turn, then read (the X measurement of QC06-01): |+> lights the same lamp every time; the 50/50 mixture of |0> and |1> still gives a coin flip; read the 0/1 way, both give 50/50. In the matrix, the mixture has lost its off-diagonal terms (line_qc_mix_jars_compare; reuse line_qc_meas_bead_jars; tape Q24-08.notes p5).

Noise is the environment measuring your qubits and telling no one (clip Q24-08 58:48-59:41): even a sealed, very cold machine still touches the outside (reuse line_qc_meas_sealed_cabinet; line_qc_mix_nosy_peek).

Why programmers meet density matrices (clip Q24-08 60:04-60:55): like static analysis of a loop that may run any number of times, you carry every outcome you cannot rule out, with its odds (line_qc_mix_every_weather).
Gates still work on a mixture: rho -> U rho U-dagger, every possibility turned the same way (60:59-62:55); this is how noise is simulated and analysed (drawn as pen work, no drawing).

Global phase (62:59-65:59; clip 65:03-65:30): multiply the whole state by a complex number of size 1 and every measurement's odds stay the same: no experiment can tell, so the two are treated as the same state (line_qc_phase_dancers, left: both dancers late by the same amount look exactly the same).

Relative phase (66:21-69:44): |+> and |-> have the same odds read the 0/1 way (50/50 each) but opposite certain answers read the +/- way: they are distinguishable because one measurement exists that tells them apart (line_qc_phase_coin_turn; line_qc_phase_dancers, right; reuse line_qc_meas_fixed_camera). 2025 touches global phase only in passing (Q25-05 43:05-43:31). Tape Q24-08.notes p6.
Takeaway: a mixture is not knowing which state; a superposition is one definite state; a global sign is nothing; a relative sign is what interference runs on (QC07-04).
Cover (line_qc_cover_06_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the nosy neighbour peeks under the cup while the experimenter looks away.
